verdict.rationale: Vue's own docs say it builds on standard HTML, CSS and JavaScript. Hands-on reports praise single-file components that separate HTML, JS and scoped styles, and describe a learning curve of minutes to hours. Some users note the template layer adds Vue-specific directive syntax (e.g. v-model), a real but secondary caveat to 'minimizing new concepts'. Missing for 10: in-depth first-party documentation of how templates map to standard HTML, and an accounting of the new directive concepts that partly offset the standard-syntax claim.

support.subject: As a developer, I can write components using standard markup, styling, and language syntax I already know, minimizing new concepts to learn

citations.quote: Builds on top of standard HTML, CSS and JavaScript with intuitive API and world-class documentation.
Single-file components separating HTML, JS and styles won them over.
You can learn the basics of Vue in minutes, and be quite adept within hours.
